claims.text: HEA components produced with standard SLM parameters typically exhibit porosity.
HEA components produced with standard SLM parameters typically exhibit dimensional inaccuracies.
HEA components produced with standard SLM parameters typically have compromised mechanical properties.
Refining laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing can promote uniform densification.
Refining laser power, scan speed, and hatch spacing can control melt-pool behavior.
Optimized SLM parameters will reduce porosity in HEA components.
Optimized SLM parameters will stabilize melt-pool dynamics.
Optimized SLM parameters will enhance interlayer bonding.
Reduced porosity, stabilized melt-pool dynamics, and enhanced interlayer bonding will improve phase homogeneity.
Optimized laser parameters reduce overheating and rapid-solidification instabilities.
Reducing overheating and rapid-solidification instabilities prevents keyhole porosity.
Reducing overheating and rapid-solidification instabilities prevents excessive residual stress.
Preventing keyhole porosity and excessive residual stress improves dimensional fidelity.
Preventing keyhole porosity and excessive residual stress improves mechanical robustness.
Compared with the baseline, optimized SLM parameters will reduce dimensional deviation.
Compared with the baseline, optimized SLM parameters will increase tensile strength.
Compared with the baseline, optimized SLM parameters will improve hardness.
The predicted improvement should hold for HEA compositions and geometries within a typical SLM processing window.
Components with extreme sizes or radically different alloy systems may not show the same level of improvement.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis states that performance is improved relative to conventionally fabricated components, whereas the baseline and predicted outcome define the comparator as HEA components made using current or conventional SLM parameters. These are potentially different comparator classes.
